overturns: Route 43's target ('show sum_sigma [y; eps, 0] is torsion in B-hat(C)') -- the element is not in ker nu, and the admissible flattenings give a non-torsion value.

gates.claim: Neumann's convention, read from the paper rather than reconstructed: R(z;p,q) = R(z) + (pi i/2)(p log(1-z) + q log z) - pi^2/6, valued in C/pi^2 Z. Routes 43-47 used a MINUS sign on the correction and omitted the -pi^2/6 per term. This gate exists so the sign is fixed in the record

ROUTE 43's ELEMENT IS NOT IN THE EXTENDED BLOCH GROUP. B-hat(C) = ker nu, and expanding nu = 0 requires X = sum(q log y + p log(1-y)) in Q*pi*i. For the eps flattening the ratio Im(X)/pi is 0.8961794846..., with no rational found at maxcoeff 1e4. So the element Route 43 proposed to show torsion is not an element of the group at all

the kernel condition forces 3q + 2p = 0 at EVERY root -- (p,q) in Z*(3,-2) -- derived from the branch relation and confirmed by search over [-4,4]^4. That is EXACTLY the null direction Route 44 found empirically and could only describe as a torsor; it is now derived from Neumann's kernel

for an admissible flattening the correction is pi^2 * k * eps, which is ZERO in C/pi^2 Z, so R is flattening-independent -- checked by shifting along the admissible direction and comparing mod pi^2. Its value is exactly -(2 pi/3) arg(y_1)

R(xi) is NOT torsion in C/pi^2 Z: arg(y_1)/pi = 0.327865386528834... and PSLQ finds no rational at maxcoeff 1e8. So the second half of Route 43's target -- 'show it is torsion' -- is false as well as inapplicable

THE TARGET, CORRECTED. Neumann's R o lambda = i(vol + i cs). R(xi) is REAL, so the volume part vanishes -- consistent with Route 42's sum_sigma D = 0 -- and the sum rule is the Chern-Simons EVALUATION cs(xi) = (2 pi/3) arg(y_1) mod pi^2. An evaluation, not a torsion statement, and in the paper's own normalisation rather than my reconstruction

verdict.condition: B-hat(C) = ker nu forces 3q + 2p = 0 at every root -- Route 44's empirical null direction, now derived.
verdict.value: R(xi) = -(2 pi/3) arg(y_1) exactly, flattening-independent mod pi^2, and not torsion.
verdict.target: the sum rule is the Chern-Simons evaluation cs(xi) = (2 pi/3) arg(y_1) mod pi^2, the volume part vanishing.
